tweetText: Travelers launched an AI Claim Assistant using OpenAI to help customers file claims anytime and manage high demand. This innovation improves customer support and streamlines operations for the insurance industry. via OpenAI News
Uber has capped employee spending on AI after exceeding its budget in just four months. This highlights the challenges companies face in managing rapid AI adoption. via TechCrunch AI

Microsoft launched a new open-source tool called Adaptive Spec-driven Scoring for AI behavior testing. This will help developers easily evaluate and improve AI models, making tech more reliable. via TechCrunch AI
Martin Scorsese is now using AI for storyboarding in his filmmaking process. This shows how even iconic directors are embracing new technology to enhance creativity. via TechCrunch AI

Microsoft just launched Scout, a new AI assistant inspired by OpenClaw, at Build. This aims to enhance the capabilities of Microsoft 365, making it more powerful and flexible for users. via TechCrunch AI

Google is launching fake call detection to combat AI deepfake impersonation scams targeting phone users. This feature is crucial for protecting people from scams that exploit trust and familiarity. via TechCrunch AI

Microsoft has launched a new specification allowing developers to set custom policies for AI agents using portable files. This gives teams better control over AI behavior, enhancing compliance and security. via TechCrunch AI.

Trump has signed a revised executive order on AI oversight, now requiring only voluntary government reviews of advanced models. This change responds to industry concerns, balancing innovation with safety. via TechCrunch AI

OpenAI has launched new Codex tools designed for various white-collar jobs like data analytics and investment banking. This will enhance productivity and streamline tasks for professionals across multiple industries. via TechCrunch AI

Anthropic is expanding its Claude Mythos program to 150 organizations in 15 countries, focusing on critical infrastructure like power and healthcare. This move aims to protect vital services from potential cyberattacks impacting millions. via TechCrunch AI
